column1: a|One of something, without saying which one.|I found a shiny shell on the beach.
about|On the subject of something.|We read a book about garden birds.
accept|To agree to take something.|Please accept this card as a thank you.
accidentally|Without meaning to do it.|I accidentally dropped my pencil under the table.
accommodate|To have enough room for someone or something.|The hall can accommodate our whole class.
according|As someone or something says.|According to the map, the park is nearby.
action|Something that someone does.|Planting a tree is an action that helps nature.
actual|Real and true.|We saw the actual footprints in the snow.
adjust|To change something a little so it fits or works.|I will adjust my helmet before riding.
admiration|A feeling of liking and respecting someone.|We watched the skilled dancer with admiration.
admission|Permission to enter a place.|Admission to the school play is free.
adorable|Very cute and easy to love.|The adorable puppy curled up in its basket.
adorably|In a very cute way.|The kitten blinked adorably at the camera.
adoration|A very strong feeling of love.|The puppy looked at its owner with adoration.
advice|Helpful ideas about what to do.|My teacher gave me advice about my drawing.
advise|To give someone a helpful idea about what to do.|Can you advise me which book to choose?
affect|To change something or make a difference to it.|Rain can affect our plans for a picnic.
afraid|Feeling scared about something.|The little rabbit was afraid of the loud noise.
age|How long someone or something has been alive.|My cousin is the same age as me.
aggressive|Behaving in a forceful or unkind way.|The story's aggressive troll would not share the bridge.
air|The mixture of gases around us that we breathe.|We went outside to breathe the fresh air.
aisle|A path between rows of seats or shelves.|We walked down the aisle to find our seats.
all|Every person or thing in a group.|All the children helped to tidy the classroom.
allowed|Given permission to do something.|We are allowed to draw after finishing our work.
aloud|In a voice that other people can hear.|Please read your favourite sentence aloud to us.
alphabet|The letters of a language in their usual order.|We sang a song to learn the alphabet.
altar|A special table used in a place of worship.|There were flowers beside the church altar.
alter|To change something.|We can alter the picture by adding a rainbow.
although|A word that joins two different or surprising ideas.|Although it was raining, we enjoyed our walk.
amateur|Someone who does an activity for enjoyment rather than as a job.|My aunt is an amateur photographer who loves birds.
ambitious|Wanting to achieve something that takes effort.|Our ambitious plan was to build a huge sandcastle.
angrily|In a way that shows someone feels angry.|The story's dragon stamped angrily on the ground.
annoy|To make someone feel a little cross.|Loud tapping can annoy someone who is reading.
anti-clockwise|Moving in the opposite direction to a clock's hands.|Turn the lid anti-clockwise to open the jar.
antique|An object that is old and often valuable.|The museum displayed an antique wooden toy.
antiseptic|Something used to clean a cut and stop germs.|The nurse used antiseptic to clean the cut.
antisocial|Not wanting company, or behaving without care for others.|The story's antisocial giant refused to join the picnic.
any|One or more, without choosing a particular one.|You may choose any book from this shelf.
applicable|Useful or suitable for a particular situation.|These playground rules are applicable to every class.
applicably|In a way that fits a particular situation.|The instructions were written applicably for both games.
application|An official request, or the act of using something.|We completed an application to join the art club.
are|Used with you, we or they to describe something.|We are ready for our spelling game.
arm|The body part between your shoulder and hand.|I raised my arm to answer the question.
around|On different sides of something, or nearby.|We sat around the table to play a game.
artificial|Made by people to look or work like something natural.|The model garden had an artificial pond.
ascent|A journey or movement upwards.|Our ascent up the hill took ten minutes.
ask|To say a question or request something.|I will ask my teacher for another pencil.
assent|To agree, or the act of agreeing.|We gave our assent to the picnic plan.
assistance|Help with doing something.|Please ask for assistance if the box is heavy.
assistant|Someone who helps another person with their work.|The shop assistant helped us find a blue coat.
astronaut|Someone trained to travel and work in space.|The astronaut waved before climbing into the rocket.
august|The eighth month of the year.|We visited the seaside during August.
author|Someone who writes a book, story or other text.|The author visited our school to read her story.
autobiography|A book someone writes about their own life.|The explorer wrote an autobiography about her adventures.
autograph|A person's name written by that person as a keepsake.|The author signed her autograph in my book.
babies|Very young children.|The babies slept quietly in their cots.
babies'|Belonging to more than one baby.|The babies' blankets were soft and warm.
back|The rear part of something, or returning to a place.|I put my name on the back of the picture.
badge|A small sign worn to show a group or achievement.|I earned a badge for learning my spellings.
badly|In a way that is not good.|The old paintbrush worked badly, so I changed it.
ball|A round object used in many games.|We kicked the ball gently across the grass.
bank|The land along the side of a river.|We watched the ducks from the river bank.
bare|Not covered by something.|The tree had bare branches in winter.
basically|In a simple way, without extra details.|The game is basically a race to collect stars.
bawl|To cry or shout very loudly.|The story's baby giant began to bawl.
be|To exist or become something.|I want to be kind to everyone.
bear|A large furry animal with a short tail.|The bear looked for berries near the trees.
beard|Hair that grows on someone's chin and cheeks.|The story's wizard had a long silver beard.
bedroom|A room where someone sleeps.|I keep my favourite books in my bedroom.
bee|A flying insect that visits flowers and can make honey.|A bee landed gently on the yellow flower.
before|Earlier than something, or in front of it.|We washed our hands before eating lunch.
behind|At the back of something.|The kitten was hiding behind the curtain.
berry|A small juicy fruit.|I picked a ripe berry from the garden bush.
better|Improved, or more good than before.|My drawing looks better with a little more colour.
blackberry|A dark juicy fruit made of small round parts.|A ripe blackberry grew beside the garden path.
blew|Moved air, or was moved by the wind.|The wind blew my hat across the playground.
blow|To move air from your mouth, or move like wind.|I can blow bubbles into the garden.
blue|The colour of a clear daytime sky.|I chose a blue ribbon for my kite.
born|Brought into the world as a baby.|The lamb was born on a sunny spring morning.
borough|A town or district with its own local council.|Our borough has a library and several parks.
both|The two people or things together.|Both of my gloves are in the drawer.
bottle|A container with a narrow neck for holding liquids.|I filled my water bottle before our walk.
bough|A large branch of a tree.|A robin perched on a low bough.
boy|A male child.|The boy helped his friend collect the pencils.
boys'|Belonging to more than one boy.|The boys' coats were hanging beside the door.
brake|Something used to slow or stop a vehicle.|I checked the brake before riding my bicycle.
bread|A food made from flour and baked.|We made fresh bread for our picnic.
bridal|Connected with a bride or a wedding.|The shop displayed a beautiful bridal bouquet.
bridge|A structure used to cross over something.|We crossed the bridge above the little stream.
bridle|Straps fitted around a horse's head to help guide it.|The rider checked the horse's bridle before setting off.
brochure|A small booklet with information and pictures.|We read a brochure about the wildlife park.
brown|A colour like wood or chocolate.|The little rabbit had soft brown fur.
bulge|A rounded part that sticks out.|There was a bulge where the book filled my bag.
burst|To break open suddenly.|The balloon burst with a loud pop.
bury|To put something under the ground and cover it.|We will bury the seeds gently in the soil.
business|Work involving making or selling things.|My aunt runs a business making wooden toys.
buzz|A low humming sound.|We heard the buzz of a bee nearby.
buzzed|Made a low humming sound.|The bee buzzed around the garden flowers.
buzzer|A device that makes a buzzing sound.|Press the buzzer when you know the answer.
buzzing|Making a low humming sound.|A bee was buzzing beside the flower pot.
by|Near something, or showing who did something.|I sat by the window with my book.
call|To speak loudly to someone, or contact them.|I will call my friend over to play.
came|Moved to a place in the past.|My friend came to our house after school.
camel|A large animal with one or two humps.|The camel walked slowly across the sandy ground.
capital|The main city of a country, or a large letter.|London is the capital of England.
car|A road vehicle usually used to carry a few people.|We travelled to the park in a car.
care|Looking after someone or something kindly.|The gardener takes care of the young plants.
carries|Holds and moves something from one place to another.|My brother carries his lunch in a small bag.
catch|To take hold of something that is moving.|Can you catch the ball with both hands?
catches|Takes hold of something that is moving.|She catches the ball before it reaches the ground.
cats|More than one small furry pet that says meow.|The cats curled up together on the blanket.
cautious|Careful to avoid trouble or danger.|We were cautious on the slippery path.
ceiling|The top inside surface of a room.|There is a bright lamp on the ceiling.
cell|A tiny part that living things are made of.|We looked at a plant cell through a microscope.
cereal|A food made from grain, often eaten for breakfast.|I had a bowl of cereal before school.
chalet|A wooden house often found in mountain areas.|We stayed in a cosy chalet beside the trees.
change|To make or become different.|Leaves change colour when autumn arrives.
changeable|Likely to change often.|The changeable weather went from sunshine to rain.
character|A person or creature in a story.|My favourite character is a kind little monster.
charge|To put electricity into a battery.|We need to charge the torch before our trip.
chef|Someone whose job is to cook food.|The chef made a colourful vegetable soup.
chemist|A scientist who studies what things are made of.|The chemist showed us how the liquid changed colour.
chief|The main or most important person in a group.|The chief gardener showed us the new greenhouse.
child|A young person.|Every child chose a book from the library.
child's|Belonging to one child.|The child's drawing was displayed on the wall.
children's|Belonging to more than one child.|The children's paintings brightened the classroom wall.
chimney|A passage that carries smoke out of a building.|A bird perched beside the tall chimney.
chorus|Part of a song that is repeated.|We all joined in with the chorus.
christmas|A winter celebration held on 25 December.|We made paper stars for Christmas.
church|A building where Christians meet to worship.|The old church had a tall stone tower.
city|A large town.|We visited a city with a big museum.
climb|To move upwards using your hands or feet.|We can climb the steps to the slide.
clothes|Things you wear on your body.|I packed warm clothes for our holiday.
clue|Information that helps you find an answer.|The footprint was a clue to the mystery.
co-operate|To work together to do something.|We will co-operate to build the model bridge.
co-ordinate|To organise things so they work well together.|We will co-ordinate our costumes for the play.
co-own|To share ownership of something.|Two neighbours co-own the small rowing boat.
coach|Someone who teaches a sport or skill.|Our coach showed us how to pass the ball.
collision|An event when two things bump into each other.|The toy cars had a collision on the track.
comfortable|Feeling relaxed and at ease.|The kitten found a comfortable place on the cushion.
comically|In a funny or amusing way.|The clown bowed comically and dropped his hat.
complement|To go well with something and make it more complete.|The blue ribbon will complement your colourful hat.
completely|In every way, with nothing left out.|We completely finished our model before lunch.
completion|The act of finishing something.|We celebrated the completion of our class puzzle.
compliment|Something kind said about someone or their work.|My friend gave me a compliment about my picture.
comprehension|Understanding something you have read or heard.|The questions checked our comprehension of the story.
conceive|To think of an idea or plan.|Can you conceive a new way to build the bridge?
confession|Saying that you did something you should not have done.|His confession explained who had hidden the biscuits.
confidence|Believing that you can do something.|Practising the song helped my confidence grow.
confident|Feeling sure that you can do something.|I feel confident about reading my story aloud.
confidential|Meant to be kept private.|The teacher kept the family's details confidential.
considerable|Quite large or great.|Building the giant model took considerable effort.
considerably|By quite a large amount.|Our sunflower grew considerably during the summer.
consideration|Careful thought about something or care for others.|We showed consideration by taking turns with the paints.
controversy|A strong disagreement about something.|There was controversy over the game's new rule.
convenience|Something being easy or useful to do.|We keep pencils nearby for convenience during lessons.
copied|Made something the same as something else.|I copied the simple shape into my notebook.
copier|A machine that makes paper copies.|The teacher put our picture in the copier.
copies|More than one version of the same thing.|We made three copies of the treasure map.
copying|Making something the same as something else.|I am copying the pattern with coloured blocks.
correspond|To exchange messages, or match something.|Our classes correspond by sending letters to each other.
cough|To push air out of your throat suddenly.|I covered my mouth when I needed to cough.
couldn't|A short way of saying could not.|I couldn't find my hat under the table.
country|An area of land with its own government.|We found our country on the classroom map.
courteous|Polite and thoughtful towards other people.|The courteous child held the door open for everyone.
crawl|To move along on your hands and knees.|We had to crawl through the play tunnel.
creature|A living animal or an imaginary living thing.|The story had a friendly purple creature.
crescent|A curved shape like a thin moon.|The moon looked like a silver crescent.
cried|Had tears because of a strong feeling.|The baby cried when her toy rolled away.
criticise|To say what you think could be better.|We can criticise an idea politely and helpfully.
cry|To have tears because of a strong feeling.|The sad part of the story made me cry.
crying|Having tears because of a strong feeling.|My friend stopped crying after a comforting hug.
cyprus's|Belonging to the country Cyprus.|Cyprus's beaches looked beautiful in the photograph.
